newsitem.title: USA: Zenith says loss narrowed in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Zenith says loss narrowed in quarter.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp., the struggling television maker, said Tuesay stronger sales and lower costs helped it narrow its loss for the latest quarter.
Zenith posted a first-quarter loss of $25.2 million, equal to 38 cents a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $35.3 million or 56 cents a share.
Zenith, whose largest stockholder is South Korea's LG Electronics Inc., with a 55 percent stake, said sales rose by 9 percent to $259 million from $237 million in 1996.

The improved results reflect the "combined effect of higher sales and lower costs resulting from the aggressive turnaround plan being implemented by Zenith's new management team," said Peter Willmott, president.
He said cost controls offset start-up problems associated with new colour picture tube production equipment at the company's Melrose Park, Ill., plant.
Zenith's colour television sales to U.S. dealers were up sharply in the quarter, despite the picture tube availability problems, the company said.
It said sales of its video cassette recorders and colour picture tubes sold to other manufacturers also increased.
Sales of Network Systems products -- such as set-top boxes and cable modems sold primarily to the cable TV industry -- were lower than a year ago.
"While the short term continues to be difficult, we are optimistic about the prospects for future revenue growth and profit improvement," Willmott said.
He said investments in Zenith's U.S. and Mexican factories are expected to boost productivity and efficiency this year.
Zenith said it is focusing on higher-margin home theatre TV systems, supported by the second-half 1997 launch of the company's first national advertising campaign in five years.
The company also plans to begin shipments in 1997 of high-resolution computer display tubes to computer monitor manufacturers, as well as new digital set-top boxes to telecommunications companies.
In early April, Zenith obtained new financing commitments that will improve the company's financial flexibility and support its turnaround strategy.
Zenith's stock was off 25 cents at $11.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
